answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the kernel schedule in the pigment ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the trellis checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 153 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 4 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
